batchName: Empire: The Five Good Emperors (AD 96-192) - Medium Batch 2

questions.question: After Nerva died in January 98, what did Trajan do before travelling to Rome?
options: Returned to his hometown in Spain
Toured the cities of Greece
Campaigned in Armenia
Inspected the Rhine and Danube frontiers
Invaded Dacia across the Danube
questions.explanation: Trajan took power smoothly but lingered on the frontiers, not entering Rome until 99. Some historians see his accession as more of a successful coup.
questions.sourceQuote: When Nerva died on 28 January 98, Trajan took power without trouble, but he lingered to inspect the Rhine and Danube frontiers before going to Rome.

questions.question: The Jewish revolt under Hadrian ended in 135 with the fall of which fortress?
options: Machaerus
Beitar
Hatra
Masada
Jotapata
questions.explanation: Beitar, about 10 km south-west of Jerusalem, fell in 135. An ancient historian put Jewish deaths at 580,000.
questions.sourceQuote: The revolt ended in 135 with the fall of Beitar, a fortress about 10 km (six miles) south-west of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What condition did Hadrian attach to adopting Antoninus as heir?
options: He must restore Trajan's lost eastern conquests
He must marry the widow of Hadrian's first heir
He must rule jointly with the Guard commander
He must finish building Hadrian's Wall in Britain
He must adopt Marcus Aurelius and the dead heir's son
questions.explanation: Antoninus had to adopt the young Marcus Aurelius and the son of Hadrian's first heir, who had died on 1 January 138. This set up the next succession in advance.
questions.sourceQuote: Hadrian then chose Antoninus, a respected senator who had governed the province of Asia, on condition that Antoninus in turn adopt two boys: the young Marcus Aurelius and the dead heir's son.

questions.question: Who signed the document adopting Hadrian as Trajan lay dying in 117?
options: The Guard commander
Trajan himself
Trajan's wife
Hadrian's guardian
The senior consul
questions.explanation: The adoption document was signed by Trajan's wife, who favoured Hadrian, not by the emperor. A Greek senator writing a century later called the adoption fake.
questions.sourceQuote: As Trajan lay dying in 117, an adoption document appeared, signed not by the emperor but by his wife, who favoured Hadrian.

questions.question: Why did Roman senators resent the peace deal Rome had earlier made with Dacia?
options: It allowed Dacians to settle freely in Italy
Rome sent the Dacian king money and experts, like tribute
It made the Dacian king a Roman senator
It banned Roman ships from the lower Danube
It gave Dacia's gold mines to Germanic tribes
questions.explanation: The Dacian king was a client king receiving Roman money and technical experts, which senators saw as shameful tribute. Dacia was an organised state rich in iron and gold.
questions.sourceQuote: Under an earlier peace deal its king was recognised as a client king (*rex amicus*) and received Roman money and technical experts, an arrangement senators saw as shameful tribute.

questions.question: What happened in 118 that the Senate never forgave Hadrian for?
options: He moved the seat of government to Athens
Four former consuls were killed without public trial
He dissolved the Senate for a whole year
He seized senators' estates to fund the frontier
He enrolled his Guard commander in the Senate
questions.explanation: Four senior former consuls, friends of Trajan and possible rivals, were condemned for conspiracy and killed. Hadrian blamed his Guard commander.
questions.sourceQuote: In 118 four senior former consuls, close friends of Trajan and possible rivals, were accused of conspiracy, condemned without a public trial and killed.

questions.question: How did the Romans bring about the fall of the Dacian capital Sarmizegetusa in 106?
options: They set it ablaze with catapults
They tunnelled under its walls
They starved it over two years
They cut the city's water pipes
They bribed the gate guards
questions.explanation: Cutting Sarmizegetusa's water supply brought the city down in 106. Its king fled and later killed himself, and his head was displayed in Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: In 106 the Romans cut the water pipes of the Dacian capital, Sarmizegetusa, and the city fell.

questions.question: What was unusual about Hadrian's report to the Senate during the Jewish revolt?
options: It named his adopted son as successor
It asked the Senate to declare war formally
It was written in Greek rather than in Latin
It announced his intention to abdicate
It omitted the line that he and the legions were well
questions.explanation: Roman losses were so heavy that Hadrian pointedly left out the customary reassurance. He summoned his best general from Britain to deal with the revolt.
questions.sourceQuote: Hadrian summoned his best general from Britain, and his report to the Senate pointedly left out the customary line that he and the legions were well.

questions.question: Which long-unfinished monument in Athens did Hadrian complete?
options: The Erechtheion
The Parthenon
Temple of Hephaestus
Theatre of Dionysus
Temple of Olympian Zeus
questions.explanation: The Temple of Olympian Zeus had been under construction for more than five centuries before Hadrian finished it. He also created a league of Greek cities centred on Athens.
questions.sourceQuote: He completed the vast Temple of Olympian Zeus in Athens, under construction for more than five centuries, and created a league of Greek cities centred there.

questions.question: How did Trajan transform the Circus Maximus, Rome's chariot-racing stadium?
options: Moved it to a new site on the Field of Mars
Replaced wooden seats with stone, adding 5,000 places
Added libraries and a market along its sides
Roofed the whole stadium with a timber awning
Converted it into an arena for gladiators
questions.explanation: Trajan rebuilt the Circus Maximus in stone and added about 5,000 places. He also built Rome's largest forum using loot from his wars.
questions.sourceQuote: He also rebuilt the Circus Maximus, Rome's chariot-racing stadium, replacing wooden seats with stone and adding about 5,000 places.
